messages.content: Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `security.delegation.tokens.renewal.retry.backoff`.

`security.delegation.tokens.renewal.retry.backoff` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT1H`. The time period how long to wait before retrying to obtain new delegation tokens after a failure.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
security.delegation.tokens.renewal.retry.backoff: PT1H
```
What does the Flink 1.20 option `state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.iter-bytes-read` configure, and how do I set it?

`state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.iter-bytes-read` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Monitor the number of uncompressed bytes read (from memtables/cache/sst) from an iterator operation in RocksDB.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.iter-bytes-read: false
```
Is `security.kerberos.tokens.renewal.time-ratio` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`security.kerberos.tokens.renewal.time-ratio` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `security.delegation.tokens.renewal.time-ratio` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `security.delegation.tokens.renewal.time-ratio`.
What does the Flink 1.20 option `high-availability.zookeeper.client.acl` configure, and how do I set it?

`high-availability.zookeeper.client.acl` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `open`. Defines the ACL (open|creator) to be configured on ZK node. The configuration value can be set to “creator” if the ZooKeeper server configuration has the “authProvider” property mapped to use SASLAuthenticationProvider and the cluster is configured to run in secure mode (Kerberos).

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
high-availability.zookeeper.client.acl: open
```
In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `scan.watermark.alignment.max-drift`?

`scan.watermark.alignment.max-drift` is an option of the Flink SQL Kafka connector (flink-connector-kafka 3.3 for Flink 1.20), type String.

It goes in the `WITH (...)` clause of `CREATE TABLE`, e.g. `'scan.watermark.alignment.max-drift' = '...'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `kubernetes.taskmanager.labels`.

`kubernetes.taskmanager.labels` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map. The labels to be set for TaskManager pods. Specified as key:value pairs separated by commas. For example, version:alphav1,deploy:test.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
kubernetes.taskmanager.labels: <value>
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.login.refresh.window.jitter`?

`sasl.login.refresh.window.jitter` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The maximum amount of random jitter relative to the credential's lifetime that is added to the login refresh thread's sleep time. Legal values are between 0 and 0.25 (25%) inclusive; a default value of 0.05 (5%) is used if no value is specified. Currently applies only to OAUTHBEARER. Type: double. Default: 0.05. Valid values: [0.0,...,0.25].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.login.refresh.window.jitter' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `request.timeout.ms`?

`request.timeout.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The configuration controls the maximum amount of time the client will wait for the response of a request. If the response is not received before the timeout elapses the client will resend the request if necessary or fail the request if retries are exhausted. This should be larger than replica.lag.time.max.ms (a broker configuration) to reduce the possibility of message duplication due to unnecessa Type: int. Default: 30000 (30 seconds). Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.request.timeout.ms' = '<value>'`.
Is `dstl.dfs.compression.enabled` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`dstl.dfs.compression.enabled` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `state.changelog.dstl.dfs.compression.enabled` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `state.changelog.dstl.dfs.compression.enabled`.
How is `gs.retry.max-rpc-timeout` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`gs.retry.max-rpc-timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
gs.retry.max-rpc-timeout: <value>
```
How is `pekko.ask.timeout` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`pekko.ask.timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT10S`. Timeout used for all futures and blocking Pekko calls. If Flink fails due to timeouts then you should try to increase this value. Timeouts can be caused by slow machines or a congested network. The timeout value requires a time-unit specifier (ms/s/min/h/d).

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
pekko.ask.timeout: PT10S
```
Is `state.backend` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?
`state.backend` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `state.backend.type` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `state.backend.type`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `max.block.ms`?

`max.block.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The configuration controls how long the KafkaProducer's send(), partitionsFor(), initTransactions(), sendOffsetsToTransaction(), commitTransaction() and abortTransaction() methods will block. For send() this timeout bounds the total time waiting for both metadata fetch and buffer allocation (blocking in the user-supplied serializers or partitioner is not counted against this timeout). For partitio Type: long. Default: 60000 (1 minute). Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.max.block.ms' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `metadata.recovery.rebootstrap.trigger.ms`?

`metadata.recovery.rebootstrap.trigger.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. If a client configured to rebootstrap using metadata.recovery.strategy=rebootstrap is unable to obtain metadata from any of the brokers in the last known metadata for this interval, client repeats the bootstrap process using bootstrap.servers configuration. Type: long. Default: 300000 (5 minutes). Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.metadata.recovery.rebootstrap.trigger.ms' = '<value>'`.
What does the Flink 1.20 option `taskmanager.network.memory.buffer-debloat.samples` configure, and how do I set it?

`taskmanager.network.memory.buffer-debloat.samples` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `20`. The number of the last buffer size values that will be taken for the correct calculation of the new one.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.network.memory.buffer-debloat.samples: 20
```
What does the Flink 1.20 option `env.java.opts.jobmanager` configure, and how do I set it?

`env.java.opts.jobmanager` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default ``. Java options to start the JVM of the JobManager with.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
env.java.opts.jobmanager: 
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `yarn.ship-files`.

`yarn.ship-files` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. A semicolon-separated list of files and/or directories to be shipped to the YARN cluster. These files/directories can come from the local path of flink client or HDFS. For example, "/path/to/local/file;/path/to/local/directory;hdfs://$namenode_address/path/of/file;hdfs://$namenode_address/path/of/directory"

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
yarn.ship-files: <value>
```
Is `state.backend.latency-track.history-size` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`state.backend.latency-track.history-size` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `state.latency-track.history-size` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `state.latency-track.history-size`.
How is `taskmanager.bind-host` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`taskmanager.bind-host` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. The local address of the network interface that the task manager binds to. If not configured, '0.0.0.0' will be used.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.bind-host: <value>
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `resourcemanager.job.timeout`.

`resourcemanager.job.timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT5M`. Timeout for jobs which don't have a job manager as leader assigned.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
resourcemanager.job.timeout: PT5M
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `metrics.internal.query-service.thread-priority`.

`metrics.internal.query-service.thread-priority` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `1`. The thread priority used for Flink's internal metric query service. The thread is created by Pekko's thread pool executor. The range of the priority is from 1 (MIN_PRIORITY) to 10 (MAX_PRIORITY). Warning, increasing this value may bring the main Flink components down.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
metrics.internal.query-service.thread-priority: 1
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `client.id`?

`client.id` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. An id string to pass to the server when making requests. The purpose of this is to be able to track the source of requests beyond just ip/port by allowing a logical application name to be included in server-side request logging. Type: string. Default: "".

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.client.id' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `value.deserializer`?

`value.deserializer` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. Deserializer class for value that implements the org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Deserializer interface. Type: class. Default: .

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.value.deserializer' = '<value>'`.
What does the Flink 1.20 option `kubernetes.taskmanager.node-selector` configure, and how do I set it?

`kubernetes.taskmanager.node-selector` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map. The node selector to be set for TaskManager pods. Specified as key:value pairs separated by commas. For example, environment:production,disk:ssd.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
kubernetes.taskmanager.node-selector: <value>
```
How is `gs.writer.chunk.size` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`gs.writer.chunk.size` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
gs.writer.chunk.size: <value>
```
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.startup.stop-on-informer-error`?

`kubernetes.operator.startup.stop-on-informer-error` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
Is `jobmanager.web.port` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?
`jobmanager.web.port` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `rest.bind-port` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `rest.bind-port`.
Is `akka.client.timeout` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?
`akka.client.timeout` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `client.timeout` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `client.timeout`.
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.resource.lifecycle.metrics.enabled`?

`kubernetes.operator.resource.lifecycle.metrics.enabled` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `python.internal.archives-key-map`.

`python.internal.archives-key-map` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
python.internal.archives-key-map: <value>
```
Is `cleanup-strategy` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?
`cleanup-strategy` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `cleanup-strategy.type` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `cleanup-strategy.type`.
How is `state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.count` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.count` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `2`. The maximum number of write buffers that are built up in memory. The default value is '2'.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.count: 2
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `sql-gateway.session.check-interval`.

`sql-gateway.session.check-interval` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT1M`.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
sql-gateway.session.check-interval: PT1M
```
What does the `maxwell-json` format option `map-null-key.mode` do in Flink 1.20 SQL?

`maxwell-json.map-null-key.mode` (type String, default `FAIL`) is an option of the `maxwell-json` format; in a table that uses `'format' = 'maxwell-json'` it is written as `'maxwell-json.map-null-key.mode' = '...'` (with `value.`/`key.` prefixes when using `value.format`/`key.format`).
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `socket.connection.setup.timeout.max.ms`?

`socket.connection.setup.timeout.max.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The maximum amount of time the client will wait for the socket connection to be established. The connection setup timeout will increase exponentially for each consecutive connection failure up to this maximum. To avoid connection storms, a randomization factor of 0.2 will be applied to the timeout resulting in a random range between 20% below and 20% above the computed value. Type: long. Default: 30000 (30 seconds).

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.socket.connection.setup.timeout.max.ms' = '<value>'`.
What does the Flink 1.20 option `state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.actual-delayed-write-rate` configure, and how do I set it?

`state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.actual-delayed-write-rate` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Monitor the current actual delayed write rate. 0 means no delay.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.actual-delayed-write-rate: false
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `execution.checkpointing.file-merging.enabled`.

`execution.checkpointing.file-merging.enabled` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Whether to enable merging multiple checkpoint files into one, which will greatly reduce the number of small checkpoint files. This is an experimental feature under evaluation, make sure you're aware of the possible effects of enabling it.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
execution.checkpointing.file-merging.enabled: false
```
How is `python.job-options` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`python.job-options` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
python.job-options: <value>
```
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.resource.metrics.enabled`?

`kubernetes.operator.resource.metrics.enabled` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `reconnect.backoff.max.ms`?

`reconnect.backoff.max.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The maximum amount of time in milliseconds to wait when reconnecting to a broker that has repeatedly failed to connect. If provided, the backoff per host will increase exponentially for each consecutive connection failure, up to this maximum. After calculating the backoff increase, 20% random jitter is added to avoid connection storms. Type: long. Default: 1000 (1 second). Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.reconnect.backoff.max.ms' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `yarn.application.priority`.

`yarn.application.priority` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `-1`. A non-negative integer indicating the priority for submitting a Flink YARN application. It will only take effect if YARN priority scheduling setting is enabled. Larger integer corresponds with higher priority. If priority is negative or set to '-1'(default), Flink will unset yarn priority setting and use cluster default priority. Please refer to YARN's official documentation for specific settings required to enable priority scheduling for the targeted YARN version.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
yarn.application.priority: -1
```
How is `blob.service.ssl.enabled` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`blob.service.ssl.enabled` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `true`. Flag to override ssl support for the blob service transport.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
blob.service.ssl.enabled: true
```
What does the Flink 1.20 option `yarn.heartbeat.container-request-interval` configure, and how do I set it?

`yarn.heartbeat.container-request-interval` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT0.5S`. Time between heartbeats with the ResourceManager if Flink requests containers: The lower this value is, the faster Flink will get notified about container allocations since requests and allocations are transmitted via heartbeats. The lower this value is, the more excessive containers might get allocated which will eventually be released but put pressure on Yarn. If you observe too many container allocations on the ResourceManager, then it is recommended to increase this value. See this link for more information.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
yarn.heartbeat.container-request-interval: PT0.5S
```
What does the Flink 1.20 option `internal.taskmanager.node-id` configure, and how do I set it?

`internal.taskmanager.node-id` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
internal.taskmanager.node-id: <value>
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.login.retry.backoff.ms`?

`sasl.login.retry.backoff.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The (optional) value in milliseconds for the initial wait between login attempts to the external authentication provider. Login uses an exponential backoff algorithm with an initial wait based on the sasl.login.retry.backoff.ms setting and will double in wait length between attempts up to a maximum wait length specified by the sasl.login.retry.backoff.max.ms setting. Currently applies only to OAUT Type: long. Default: 100.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.login.retry.backoff.ms' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `taskmanager.runtime.hashjoin-bloom-filters`.

`taskmanager.runtime.hashjoin-bloom-filters` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Flag to activate/deactivate bloom filters in the hybrid hash join implementation. In cases where the hash join needs to spill to disk (datasets larger than the reserved fraction of memory), these bloom filters can greatly reduce the number of spilled records, at the cost some CPU cycles.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.runtime.hashjoin-bloom-filters: false
```
Is `taskmanager.debug.memory.startLogThread` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`taskmanager.debug.memory.startLogThread` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `taskmanager.debug.memory.log` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `taskmanager.debug.memory.log`.
What does the `maxwell-json` format option `timestamp-format.standard` do in Flink 1.20 SQL?

`maxwell-json.timestamp-format.standard` (type String, default `SQL`) is an option of the `maxwell-json` format; in a table that uses `'format' = 'maxwell-json'` it is written as `'maxwell-json.timestamp-format.standard' = '...'` (with `value.`/`key.` prefixes when using `value.format`/`key.format`).
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `blob.storage.directory`.

`blob.storage.directory` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. The config parameter defining the local storage directory to be used by the blob server. If not configured, then it will default to <WORKING_DIR>/blobStorage.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
blob.storage.directory: <value>
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `cleanup.policy`?

`cleanup.policy` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. This config designates the retention policy to use on log segments. The "delete" policy (which is the default) will discard old segments when their retention time or size limit has been reached. The "compact" policy will enable log compaction, which retains the latest value for each key. It is also possible to specify both policies in a comma-separated list (e.g. "delete,compact"). In this case, o Type: list. Default: delete. Valid values: [compact, delete].

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config cleanup.policy=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
How is `taskmanager.rpc.port` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`taskmanager.rpc.port` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `0`. The external RPC port where the TaskManager is exposed. Accepts a list of ports (“50100,50101”), ranges (“50100-50200”) or a combination of both. It is recommended to set a range of ports to avoid collisions when multiple TaskManagers are running on the same machine.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.rpc.port: 0
```
How is `table.exec.async-scalar.timeout` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`table.exec.async-scalar.timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT3M`.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
table.exec.async-scalar.timeout: PT3M
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `taskmanager.memory.network.min`.

`taskmanager.memory.network.min` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize with default `64 mb`. Min Network Memory size for TaskExecutors. Network Memory is off-heap memory reserved for ShuffleEnvironment (e.g., network buffers). Network Memory size is derived to make up the configured fraction of the Total Flink Memory. If the derived size is less/greater than the configured min/max size, the min/max size will be used. The exact size of Network Memory can be explicitly specified by setting the min/max to the same value.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.memory.network.min: 64 mb
```
In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `value.format`?

`value.format` is an option of the Flink SQL Kafka connector (flink-connector-kafka 3.3 for Flink 1.20), type String. The format used to deserialize and serialize the value part of Kafka messages. Please refer to the formats page for more details and more format options. Note: Either this option or the 'format' option are required.

It goes in the `WITH (...)` clause of `CREATE TABLE`, e.g. `'value.format' = '...'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `state.changelog.dstl.dfs.base-path`.

`state.changelog.dstl.dfs.base-path` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. Base path to store changelog files.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
state.changelog.dstl.dfs.base-path: <value>
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `metrics.recording.level`?

`metrics.recording.level` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The highest recording level for metrics. It has three levels for recording metrics - info, debug, and trace. INFO level records only essential metrics necessary for monitoring system performance and health. It collects vital data without gathering too much detail, making it suitable for production environments where minimal overhead is desired.DEBUG level records most metrics, providing more detai Type: string. Default: INFO. Valid values: [INFO, DEBUG, TRACE].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.metrics.recording.level' = '<value>'`.
How is `yarn.view.acls` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`yarn.view.acls` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. Users and groups to give VIEW access. The ACLs are of for comma-separated-users<space>comma-separated-groups. Wildcard ACL is also supported. The only valid wildcard ACL is *, which grants permission to all users and groups.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
yarn.view.acls: <value>
```
Is `taskmanager.max-registration-pause` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`taskmanager.max-registration-pause` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `taskmanager.registration.max-backoff` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `taskmanager.registration.max-backoff`.
How is `kubernetes.artifacts.local-upload-enabled` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`kubernetes.artifacts.local-upload-enabled` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Enables uploading 'local://' schemed artifacts to DFS before the the application cluster deployment.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
kubernetes.artifacts.local-upload-enabled: false
```
How is `state.changelog.dstl.dfs.discard.num-threads` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`state.changelog.dstl.dfs.discard.num-threads` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `1`. Number of threads to use to discard changelog (e.g. pre-emptively uploaded unused state).

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
state.changelog.dstl.dfs.discard.num-threads: 1
```
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.dynamic.namespaces.enabled`?

`kubernetes.operator.dynamic.namespaces.enabled` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
How is `table.exec.async-lookup.timeout` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`table.exec.async-lookup.timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT3M`.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
table.exec.async-lookup.timeout: PT3M
```
In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `format`?

`format` is an option of the Flink SQL Kafka connector (flink-connector-kafka 3.3 for Flink 1.20), type String. The format used to deserialize and serialize the value part of Kafka messages. Please refer to the formats page for more details and more format options. Note: Either this option or the 'value.format' option are required.

It goes in the `WITH (...)` clause of `CREATE TABLE`, e.g. `'format' = '...'`.
Is `job-manager.max-attempts-history-size` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

`job-manager.max-attempts-history-size` is deprecated in Flink 1.20; use `jobmanager.execution.attempts-history-size` instead. The deprecated key is still read as a fallback, but new configurations should use `jobmanager.execution.attempts-history-size`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `isolation.level`?

`isolation.level` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. Controls how to read messages written transactionally. If set to read_committed, consumer.poll() will only return transactional messages which have been committed. If set to read_uncommitted (the default), consumer.poll() will return all messages, even transactional messages which have been aborted. Non-transactional messages will be returned unconditionally in either mode. Messages will always be Type: string. Default: read_uncommitted. Valid values: [read_committed, read_uncommitted].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.isolation.level' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `client.heartbeat.timeout`.

`client.heartbeat.timeout` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT3M`. Cancel the job if the dispatcher hasn't received the client's heartbeat after timeout when 'execution.attached' and 'execution.shutdown-on-attached-exit' are both true.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
client.heartbeat.timeout: PT3M
```
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `autoscaler.standalone.control-loop.parallelism`?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `table.optimizer.runtime-filter.min-filter-ratio` configure, and how do I set it?

What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `ssl.keystore.password`?

How is `table.optimizer.runtime-filter.enabled` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `properties.group.id`?

In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `scan.bounded.timestamp-millis`?

`scan.bounded.timestamp-millis` is an option of the Flink SQL Kafka connector (flink-connector-kafka 3.3 for Flink 1.20), type Long. End at the specified epoch timestamp (milliseconds) used in case of 'timestamp' bounded mode.

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `partitioner.adaptive.partitioning.enable`?

When set to 'true', the producer will try to adapt to broker performance and produce more messages to partitions hosted on faster brokers. If 'false', the producer will try to distribute messages uniformly. Note: this setting has no effect if a custom partitioner is used. Type: boolean. Default: true.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.partitioner.adaptive.partitioning.enable' = '<value>'`.
How is `interval` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `task.cancellation.interval` configure, and how do I set it?

Is `taskmanager.network.memory.min` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the `csv` format option `field-delimiter` do in Flink 1.20 SQL?

`csv.field-delimiter` (type String, default `,`) is an option of the `csv` format; in a table that uses `'format' = 'csv'` it is written as `'csv.field-delimiter' = '...'` (with `value.`/`key.` prefixes when using `value.format`/`key.format`).
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.scope`?

`sasl.oauthbearer.scope` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. This is the level of access a client application is granted to a resource or API which is included in the token request. If provided, it should match one or more scopes configured in the identity provider. Type: string. Default: null.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.oauthbearer.scope' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.refresh.ms`?

`sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.refresh.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The (optional) value in milliseconds for the broker to wait between refreshing its JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) cache that contains the keys to verify the signature of the JWT. Type: long. Default: 3600000 (1 hour).

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.refresh.ms' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `table.exec.resource.hash-join.memory`.

`table.exec.resource.hash-join.memory` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize with default `128 mb`.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
table.exec.resource.hash-join.memory: 128 mb
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.claim.jti.include`?

`sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.claim.jti.include` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. Flag that determines if the JWT assertion should generate a unique ID for the JWT and include it in the jti (JWT ID) claim. Type: boolean. Default: false.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.claim.jti.include' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `restart-strategy.failure-rate.max-failures-per-interval`.

`restart-strategy.failure-rate.max-failures-per-interval` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `1`. Maximum number of restarts in given time interval before failing a job if restart-strategy.type has been set to failure-rate .

What does the Flink 1.20 option `table.column-expansion-strategy` configure, and how do I set it?

`table.column-expansion-strategy` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type TableConfigOptions.ColumnExpansionStrategy with default `[]`. Allowed values: EXCLUDE_ALIASED_VIRTUAL_METADATA_COLUMNS, EXCLUDE_DEFAULT_VIRTUAL_METADATA_COLUMNS.

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `ssl.cipher.suites`?

`ssl.cipher.suites` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. A list of cipher suites. This is a named combination of authentication, encryption, MAC and key exchange algorithm used to negotiate the security settings for a network connection using TLS or SSL network protocol. By default all the available cipher suites are supported. Type: list. Default: null.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.ssl.cipher.suites' = '<value>'`.
How is `security.ssl.rest.truststore-type` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`security.ssl.rest.truststore-type` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `pkcs12`. The type of the truststore for Flink's external REST endpoints.

Is `restart-strategy` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `env.hbase.conf.dir` configure, and how do I set it?

What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `flush.ms`?

`flush.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. This setting allows specifying a time interval at which we will force an fsync of data written to the log. For example if this was set to 1000 we would fsync after 1000 ms had passed. Note that this setting depends on the broker-level configuration log.flush.scheduler.interval.ms, which controls how frequently the flush check occurs. In general we recommend you not set this and use replication for Type: long. Default: 9223372036854775807. Valid values: [0,...].

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config flush.ms=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `file.delete.delay.ms`?

`file.delete.delay.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. The time to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem Type: long. Default: 60000 (1 minute). Valid values: [0,...].

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config file.delete.delay.ms=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
How is `yarn.application.type` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`yarn.application.type` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. A custom type for your YARN application..

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
yarn.application.type: <value>
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `python.client.executable`.

`python.client.executable` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `python`.

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.observer.rest-ready.delay`?

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.clock.skew.seconds`?

`sasl.oauthbearer.clock.skew.seconds` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The (optional) value in seconds to allow for differences between the time of the OAuth/OIDC identity provider and the broker. Type: int. Default: 30.

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `autoscaler.standalone.jdbc.username`?

`autoscaler.standalone.jdbc.username` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `rest.url-prefix`.

`rest.url-prefix` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `/`.

```yaml
rest.url-prefix: /
```
Is `local.number-taskmanager` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `execution.checkpointing.checkpoints-after-tasks-finish` configure, and how do I set it?

`execution.checkpointing.checkpoints-after-tasks-finish` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `true`. Feature toggle for enabling checkpointing even if some of tasks have finished. Before you enable it, please take a look at the important considerations

In a Flink 1.20 SQL `CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('connector' = 'kafka', ...)`, what is the option `topic-pattern`?

`topic-pattern` is an option of the Flink SQL Kafka connector (flink-connector-kafka 3.3 for Flink 1.20), type String. The regular expression for a pattern of topic names to read from or write to. All topics with names that match the specified regular expression will be subscribed by the consumer when the job starts running. For sinks, the `topic` metadata column is writable, must be provided and match the `topic-pattern` regex. Note, only one of "topic-pattern" and "topic" can be specified.

It goes in the `WITH (...)` clause of `CREATE TABLE`, e.g. `'topic-pattern' = '...'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.sub.claim.name`?

`sasl.oauthbearer.sub.claim.name` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The OAuth claim for the subject is often named "sub", but this (optional) setting can provide a different name to use for the subject included in the JWT payload's claims if the OAuth/OIDC provider uses a different name for that claim. Type: string. Default: sub.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.oauthbearer.sub.claim.name' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `security.protocol`?

`security.protocol` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. Protocol used to communicate with brokers. Type: string. Default: PLAINTEXT. Valid values: (case insensitive) [SASL_SSL, PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.security.protocol' = '<value>'`.
How is `env.log.dir` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`env.log.dir` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. Defines the directory where the Flink logs are saved. It has to be an absolute path. (Defaults to the log directory under Flink’s home)

```yaml
env.log.dir: <value>
```

How is `state.backend.rocksdb.metrics.compaction-pending` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.kerberos.kinit.cmd`?

`sasl.kerberos.kinit.cmd` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. Kerberos kinit command path. Type: string. Default: /usr/bin/kinit.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.sasl.kerberos.kinit.cmd' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `security.ssl.internal.truststore-type`.

`security.ssl.internal.truststore-type` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `pkcs12`. The type of truststore for Flink's internal endpoints (rpc, data transport, blob server).

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.savepoint.trigger.grace-period`?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `pipeline.classpaths` configure, and how do I set it?

`pipeline.classpaths` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. A semicolon-separated list of the classpaths to package with the job jars to be sent to the cluster. These have to be valid URLs.

Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `scope.variables.additional`.

`scope.variables.additional` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map with default `{}`.

How is `high-availability.kubernetes.leader-election.renew-deadline` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`high-availability.kubernetes.leader-election.renew-deadline` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration with default `PT15S`. ```
What does the Flink 1.20 option `rest.bind-port` configure, and how do I set it?

`rest.bind-port` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `8081`. The port that the server binds itself. Accepts a list of ports (“50100,50101”), ranges (“50100-50200”) or a combination of both. It is recommended to set a range of ports to avoid collisions when multiple Rest servers are running on the same machine.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
rest.bind-port: 8081
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `table.builtin-database-name`.

`table.builtin-database-name` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `default_database`.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
table.builtin-database-name: default_database
```
How is `taskmanager.system-out.log.cache-upper-size` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`taskmanager.system-out.log.cache-upper-size` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize with default `100 kb`. The cache upper size when Flink caches current line context of System.out or System.err when taskmanager.system-out.mode is LOG.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.system-out.log.cache-upper-size: 100 kb
```
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `table.exec.local-hash-agg.adaptive.enabled`.

`table.exec.local-hash-agg.adaptive.enabled` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `true`.

What does the Flink 1.20 option `taskmanager.network.request-backoff.max` configure, and how do I set it?

`taskmanager.network.request-backoff.max` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `10000`. Maximum backoff in milliseconds for partition requests of local input channels.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
taskmanager.network.request-backoff.max: 10000
```
How is `historyserver.web.address` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`historyserver.web.address` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. Address of the HistoryServer's web interface.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml
historyserver.web.address: <value>
```
What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `remote.log.delete.on.disable`?

`remote.log.delete.on.disable` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. Determines whether tiered data for a topic should be deleted after tiered storage is disabled on a topic. This configuration should be enabled when trying to set `remote.storage.enable` from true to false Type: boolean. Default: false.

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config remote.log.delete.on.disable=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.josdk.metrics.enabled`?

`kubernetes.operator.josdk.metrics.enabled` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `high-availability.zookeeper.path.jobgraphs`.

`high-availability.zookeeper.path.jobgraphs` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `/jobgraphs`. ZooKeeper root path (ZNode) for job graphs

Is `akka.framesize` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

Is `jobmanager.adaptive-batch-scheduler.max-parallelism` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `taskmanager.network.memory.buffer-debloat.target`.

What does the Flink 1.20 option `taskmanager.memory.segment-size` configure, and how do I set it?

`taskmanager.memory.segment-size` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize with default `32 kb`. Size of memory buffers used by the network stack and the memory manager.

Is `jobmanager.adaptive-batch-scheduler.avg-data-volume-per-task` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `taskmanager.network.netty.client.tcp.keepIntervalSec` configure, and how do I set it?

How is `table.resources.download-dir` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`table.resources.download-dir` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String with default `/tmp`.

What does the Flink 1.20 option `sql-gateway.worker.threads.min` configure, and how do I set it?

`sql-gateway.worker.threads.min` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Integer with default `5`.

How is `taskmanager.load-balance.mode` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

How is `pekko.remote-fork-join-executor.parallelism-max` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

How is `flink.yarn.<key>` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `metrics.recording.level`?

`metrics.recording.level` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The highest recording level for metrics. It has three levels for recording metrics - info, debug, and trace. INFO level records only essential metrics necessary for monitoring system performance and health. It collects vital data without gathering too much detail, making it suitable for production environments where minimal overhead is desired.DEBUG level records most metrics, providing more detai Type: string. Default: INFO. Valid values: [INFO, DEBUG, TRACE].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.metrics.recording.level' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `retry.backoff.ms`?

`retry.backoff.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The amount of time to wait before attempting to retry a failed request to a given topic partition. This avoids repeatedly sending requests in a tight loop under some failure scenarios. This value is the initial backoff value and will increase exponentially for each failed request, up to the retry.backoff.max.ms value. Type: long. Default: 100. Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.retry.backoff.ms' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `reconnect.backoff.max.ms`?

`reconnect.backoff.max.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The maximum amount of time in milliseconds to wait when reconnecting to a broker that has repeatedly failed to connect. If provided, the backoff per host will increase exponentially for each consecutive connection failure, up to this maximum. After calculating the backoff increase, 20% random jitter is added to avoid connection storms. Type: long. Default: 1000 (1 second). Valid values: [0,...].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.reconnect.backoff.max.ms' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `rest.flamegraph.enabled`.

`rest.flamegraph.enabled` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Boolean with default `false`. Enables the experimental flame graph feature.

```yaml

```
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.login.refresh.buffer.seconds`?

`sasl.login.refresh.buffer.seconds` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The amount of buffer time before credential expiration to maintain when refreshing a credential, in seconds. If a refresh would otherwise occur closer to expiration than the number of buffer seconds then the refresh will be moved up to maintain as much of the buffer time as possible. Legal values are between 0 and 3600 (1 hour); a default value of 300 (5 minutes) is used if no value is specified. Type: short. Default: 300. Valid values: [0,...,3600].

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `ssl.engine.factory.class`?

What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `follower.replication.throttled.replicas`?

`follower.replication.throttled.replicas` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. A list of replicas for which log replication should be throttled on the follower side. The list should describe a set of replicas in the form [PartitionId]:[BrokerId],[PartitionId]:[BrokerId]:... or alternatively the wildcard '*' can be used to throttle all replicas for this topic. Type: list. Default: "". Valid values: [partitionId]:[brokerId],[partitionId]:[brokerId],....

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config follower.replication.throttled.replicas=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `historyserver.archive.fs.dir`.

`historyserver.archive.fs.dir` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type String. Comma separated list of directories to fetch archived jobs from. In `config.yaml`:

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `compression.lz4.level`?

`compression.lz4.level` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The compression level to use if compression.type is set to lz4. Type: int. Default: 9. Valid values: [1,...,17].

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.compression.lz4.level' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `remote.storage.enable`?

`remote.storage.enable` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 topic-level configuration. To enable tiered storage for a topic, set this configuration to true. To disable tiered storage for a topic that has it enabled, set this configuration to false. When disabling, you must also set remote.log.delete.on.disable to true. Type: boolean. Default: false.

Set it at topic creation with `kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server <host:port> --create --topic <name> --config remote.storage.enable=<value>`, or in a Strimzi `KafkaTopic` under `spec.config`.
Can I still create Kafka 4.1 topics with `kafka-topics.sh --zookeeper`?

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `kubernetes.operator.leader-election.retry-period`?

Is `recovery.zookeeper.path.jobgraphs` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `env.java.default-opts.all` configure, and how do I set it?

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.jwt.retriever.class`?

Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `python.map-state.iterate-response-batch-size`.

What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.login.read.timeout.ms`?

How is `state.backend.rocksdb.checkpoint.transfer.thread.num` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `pekko.retry-gate-closed-for` configure, and how do I set it?

What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `metadata.max.age.ms`?

`metadata.max.age.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. `transaction.timeout.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The maximum amount of time in milliseconds that a transaction will remain open before the coordinator proactively aborts it. The start of the transaction is set at the time that the first partition is added to it. If this value is larger than the transaction.max.timeout.ms setting in the broker, the request will fail with a InvalidTxnTimeoutException error. Type: int. Default: 60000 (1 minute).

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.transaction.timeout.ms' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `state.backend.rocksdb.memory.write-buffer-ratio`.

`state.backend.rocksdb.memory.write-buffer-ratio` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Double with default `0.5`. What does the Flink 1.20 option `sql-gateway.session.idle-timeout` configure, and how do I set it?

What is the Kafka 4.1 topic-level setting `message.timestamp.type`?

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `job.autoscaler.vertex.exclude.ids`?

`job.autoscaler.vertex.exclude.ids` is a Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 configuration option. It can be set in the operator's configuration or per deployment in `FlinkDeployment.spec.flinkConfiguration`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `ssl.truststore.certificates`?

`ssl.truststore.certificates` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. Trusted certificates in the format specified by 'ssl.truststore.type'. Default SSL engine factory supports only PEM format with X.509 certificates. Type: password. Default: null.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.ssl.truststore.certificates' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `partitioner.class`?

`partitioner.class` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. Determines which partition to send a record to when records are produced. Available options are:If not set, the default partitioning logic is used. This strategy send records to a partition until at least batch.size bytes is produced to the partition. It works with the strategy:If no partition is specified but a key is present, choose a partition based on a hash of the key.If no partition or key i Type: class. Default: null.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.partitioner.class' = '<value>'`.
What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `ssl.enabled.protocols`?

`ssl.enabled.protocols` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 consumer configuration. The list of protocols enabled for SSL connections. The default is 'TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3'. This means that clients and servers will prefer TLSv1.3 if both support it and fallback to TLSv1.2 otherwise (assuming both support at least TLSv1.2). This default should be fine for most use cases. Also see the config documentation for `ssl.protocol` to understand how it can impact the TLS version negotiation beh Type: list. Default: TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3.

In a Flink SQL Kafka table it is passed as `'properties.ssl.enabled.protocols' = '<value>'`.
Explain the Apache Flink 1.20 configuration key `taskmanager.memory.network.max`.

`taskmanager.memory.network.max` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type MemorySize with default `9223372036854775807 bytes`. Max Network Memory size for TaskExecutors. Network Memory is off-heap memory reserved for ShuffleEnvironment (e.g., network buffers). Network Memory size is derived to make up the configured fraction of the Total Flink Memory. If the derived size is less/greater than the configured min/max size, the min/max size will be used. By default, the max limit of Network Memory is Long.MAX_VALUE. The exact size of Network Memory can be explicitly specified by setting the min/max to the same value.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml

```
How is `pipeline.jobvertex-parallelism-overrides` used in a Flink 1.20 cluster configuration?

`pipeline.jobvertex-parallelism-overrides` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Map with default `{}`. A parallelism override map (jobVertexId -> parallelism) which will be used to update the parallelism of the corresponding job vertices of submitted JobGraphs.

Is `execution.savepoint-restore-mode` still the right Flink configuration key in Flink 1.20?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `sql-gateway.worker.threads.max` configure, and how do I set it?

What does the Flink 1.20 option `resourcemanager.standalone.start-up-time` configure, and how do I set it?

`resourcemanager.standalone.start-up-time` is an Apache Flink 1.20 configuration option of type Duration. Time of the start-up period of a standalone cluster. During this time, resource manager of the standalone cluster expects new task executors to be registered, and will not fail slot requests that can not be satisfied by any current registered slots. After this time, it will fail pending and new coming requests immediately that can not be satisfied by registered slots. If not set, slot.request.timeout will be used by default.

In `config.yaml`:
```yaml

```
What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.claim.nbf.seconds`?

Where do I set the Flink Kubernetes Operator option `job.autoscaler.memory.tuning.enabled`?

What is the Kafka 4.1 consumer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.claim.exp.seconds`?

`linger.ms` is an Apache Kafka 4.1 producer configuration. The producer groups together any records that arrive in between request transmissions into a single batched request. Normally this occurs only under load when records arrive faster than they can be sent out. However in some circumstances the client may want to reduce the number of requests even under moderate load. What is the Kafka 4.1 producer setting `sasl.oauthbearer.expected.audience`?
